model.name: Survey / Questionnaire
model.purpose: Represent one governed questionnaire or survey instrument so agents can understand exactly what may be asked, in which form, order, language, mode and context, without confusing an instrument definition with a study, administration or person's response.
model.scope_statement: Owns instrument identity, versions and lifecycle; purpose, concepts, variables and intended population; modules, sections, questions, statements, instructions and stimuli; response domains, options, scales, units, validation and missing states; ordering, routing, randomization and calculation; language, translation, presentation, mode and accessibility variants; testing, review, approval and limitation evidence; non-owning study, campaign, wave, sample, consent, administration, response and dataset bindings; publication, privacy, access, retention, provenance, correction and projections. Individual respondents, answers, observations, datasets and analysis results remain external where authoritative.
in_scope: Instrument identity, versions, purpose, population, components, questions, instructions, response domains, logic, language, presentation, modes and accessibility
Testing, quality, approvals, privacy, administration and output bindings, lifecycle, correction, records and interoperability projections
out_of_scope: Owning Study, Program, Campaign, Wave, Administration, Interview, Respondent, Consent, Sample, Response, Observation, Dataset, Analysis, Audit or Records masters
Treating a permitted response as evidence that a question was asked, understood, answered, truthful, complete or comparable

Autonomous respondent contact, instrument publication, ethics or consent approval, sampling changes, answer collection, protected-trait inference, identity linkage, access widening, dataset creation, result certification or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unfrozen parent signal may identify a record or collection context, but no approved relation row exists and it grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Study, program, campaign, wave and administration
boundary_notes.distinction: These objects define research intent and actual collection activity. The instrument owns reusable questions and logic and stores only non-owning use bindings.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Respondent, consent, sample, response, observation, dataset and analysis result
boundary_notes.distinction: These masters carry people, authority, selection, actual answers, observed facts and outputs. The instrument defines permitted capture structures only.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Question, response domain, variable and controlled concept
boundary_notes.distinction: Question content, permitted value domain, statistical variable and controlled concept remain separately identifiable and versioned even when bundled into one instrument.

boundary_notes.neighbor: DDI, GSIM, GSBPM, ISO 20252, FHIR, Census, Statistics Canada, GOV.UK, WCAG, DPV, PROV, SKOS and IETF profiles
boundary_notes.distinction: Each source has a distinct scope and normative force. Every mapping is version-pinned, profile-qualified and loss-declaring.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension owner, namespace authority, research governance mandate and accountable instrument owner
Authoritative Instrument, Study, Program, Campaign, Wave, Administration, Interview, Respondent, Consent, Sample, Response, Dataset, Variable, Analysis, Audit and Records registries
Approved questionnaire, terminology, language, translation, mode, accessibility, validation, testing, ethics, privacy, access, retention and interoperability profiles
Role, delegation, review, publication, correction, withdrawal and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint instrument, version, module, item, question, response-domain, option, rule, presentation, test, use-binding, correction and projection IDs; preserve every external master identifier.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize an instrument by authoritative instrument identifier and owner namespace, never by title, wording, URL, date or file digest alone.
Keep instrument, study, campaign, wave, administration, interview, respondent, consent, sample, response, observation, dataset and result independently identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare question, response-domain, logic, language, mode, accessibility, testing, privacy, lifecycle and interoperability effects.
Published instrument versions are immutable; changes create linked successors with reason, compatibility, migration and review.
Never silently change wording, intent, concept, population, response domain, option code, missing state, routing, randomization, calculation, language, mode, accessibility or consent binding.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, semantics, permitted answers, logic, presentation, authority, time, privacy and provenance survive.
Every projection pins standard, vocabulary, schema, language, mode and mapping versions and declares information loss.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for each instrument, version, component, question, domain, rule or artifact, qualified by issuer, namespace and record kind.
Governed globally resolvable instrument or question IRI.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish reference, test, approval, effective, administration, response, publication, modification, correction, recorded, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, record kind, instrument and population scope, profile versions, actor, event and knowledge times, confidentiality marking and provenance.

policies: The instrument owns questions, permitted-response structures, logic, presentation variants, test evidence and version lineage but not study, collection, respondent, consent, response, dataset, analysis, audit or records masters.
A question defines what may be asked and answered; it is never evidence that it was asked, understood, answered truthfully or observed as fact.
Wording, language, presentation, mode, order, routing and version can change meaning or comparability and must remain explicit.

Agents cannot autonomously contact respondents, publish instruments, approve ethics or consent, change samples, collect answers, infer protected traits, link identities, widen access, create datasets, certify results or dispose records without delegated authority.

read: Resolve instrument head, purpose, population, components, questions, domains, logic, language, modes, accessibility, tests, approvals, use bindings, lifecycle and projection loss under the permitted view.
create: Bind stable identity, owner, purpose, population, semantics, response domains, source authority and initial lifecycle before applied use.
update: Append successor components, questions, domains, logic, translations, presentation variants, tests, reviews, approvals, corrections and lifecycle assertions with reason, authority, expected revision, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply legal hold, scientific reproducibility, respondent protection, privacy, security and adopting-Dimension records policy; withdraw or tombstone only the instrument view without cascading to study, response, dataset, audit or records masters, and let authoritative systems execute physical disposition.

roles.name: Instrument owner
responsibilities: Own purpose, scope, population, lifecycle, compatibility and accountable use.

roles.name: Questionnaire designer
responsibilities: Own wording, components, response domains, instructions, routing, presentation and mode variants.

roles.name: Survey methodologist
responsibilities: Own construct validity, testing, bias, burden, equivalence, sampling-use and measurement limitations.

roles.name: Terminology and translation steward
responsibilities: Own concepts, classifications, code lists, language tags, translations, equivalence and fallbacks.

roles.name: Accessibility reviewer
responsibilities: Review perceivability, operability, understandability, robustness, accommodations and mode-specific evidence.

roles.name: Ethics, privacy and access authority
responsibilities: Own purpose, consent, minimization, sensitive-question, confidentiality, access and disclosure policies.

roles.name: Publication and records steward
responsibilities: Own review, approval, publication, correction, withdrawal, retention, tombstone, audit and projection policy.

access.default_rule: Deny protected question rationales, unreleased instruments, sampling or anti-fraud logic, respondent identifiers, consent details, answers, sensitive-trait mappings, credentials and restricted test evidence unless a purpose-bound policy permits the minimum necessary view.
exceptions: Declared research, safety, incident, privacy, legal, audit or subject-rights access must cite authority, scope, purpose and time limit and must be logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, instrument and version, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected components, source revision and outcome without duplicating respondent data.

read_order: Read Dimension research governance, namespace, questionnaire, study, consent, privacy, access, retention and agent policies.
Read this instrument and linked study, campaign, wave, administration, respondent, consent, sample, response, dataset, variable, analysis, audit and records models before mutation.

coverage.claim: WM-DAT-009 covers one governed questionnaire or survey instrument from identity, purpose and population through components, questions, response domains, validation, routing, presentation, language, modes, accessibility, testing, privacy, administration bindings, output schemas, lifecycle and projections. Domain profiles, restricted ISO clauses and independent external review remain deferred.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
No relation row is frozen; the WM-REC-007 parent signal grants no approved ownership or cascade behavior.
Adaptive testing, psychometrics, clinical outcome instruments, educational assessment, election polling and jurisdiction-specific ethics require separate profiles.
ISO 20252:2026 is used only from public scope and lifecycle metadata; access-restricted requirements were not inferred.
conflicts: Survey study, questionnaire instrument, campaign, wave, administration, interview, respondent, consent, sample, response, observation, dataset and analysis result are not interchangeable identities.
Permitted answer, initial value, prefill, calculated value, actual answer, derived dataset value and analyst inference are distinct.
Missing, do not know, refusal, not applicable, not asked, invalid, incomplete and nonresponse require distinct states.
regional_assumptions: Consent, ethics, sensitive questions, accessibility, respondent rights, record retention and disclosure depend on jurisdiction, population and organization.
FHIR is healthcare Trial Use; Census, Statistics Canada, GOV.UK, AAPOR and GSBPM are sector or jurisdiction profiles and none is universal.
adversarial_checks: Reject a package that collapses instrument identity with a study, administration or response.
Reject a question without stable identity, version, wording, intent, response domain, population, language, mode and provenance.
Reject inference that an allowed answer was actually asked, selected, truthful, complete or comparable.

Reject autonomous respondent contact, publication, ethics approval, consent, sampling change, collection, trait inference, identity linkage, access widening, dataset creation, result certification or disposition.
Reject a projection that hides wording, language, mode, routing, missing-state or version differences.
